newsitem.title: USA: Section of California highway buckles, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Section of California highway buckles, no injuries.

text.p: Traffic on a busy California highway was disrupted Tuesday when a bridge over the Salinas River buckled, state officials said.

One span of the 466-foot (140 metre) bridge on Highway 101 -- one of the state's main north-south routes -- gave way near Soledad, about 60 miles (100 km) south of San Jose, California Department of Transportation spokesman Jim Drago said.
There were no injuries but officials immediately stopped traffic from crossing the bridge while they assessed the damage.
Later, vehicles traveling south were allowed to cross the bridge at slow speeds. The northbound section remained closed and traffic was diverted onto a county road.
Drago said it was not immediately clear what caused the bridge, built in 1938, to buckle. "Our engineers are at the bridge," he said.
Officials said they were looking into the possibility that the fast-moving Salinas River had undermined the structure. Persistent rains have swollen rivers across the state.
